sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Header note on shared constants
sections.what: A comment only. It says these lists hold no database code, so the front end can use them directly, while the back end uses the full schema file.
sections.why: The comment states the reason: keep database tools out of front-end code.
sections.watch_out: Because the full schema lives elsewhere, the two copies can drift apart with no check.

sections.name: COMPANY_TYPES
sections.title: Allowed company types
sections.what: Lists the twelve kinds of organization a company record may be, such as owner, EPC contractor, regulator, media and association.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond setting which values a company may take.
sections.watch_out: Adding a type here does not add it to the backend, so the two lists must be updated together.

sections.name: PROJECT_ROLES
sections.title: Allowed project roles
sections.what: Lists the seventeen roles a party can play in a project, such as owner, operator, EPC contractor, reactor vendor and grid connection provider.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: This list differs from the role list in the industry settings file, which has roles such as equipment supplier and offtaker that this list lacks, so the two can disagree.

sections.name: ROLE_LABELS
sections.title: Display labels and definitions for roles
sections.what: Gives each role a plain label and a one-line definition, for example turning the key for EPC into EPC Contractor. It also includes company types that are not project roles, such as association and media.
sections.why: Likely reason: users see readable names and definitions instead of internal keys.
sections.watch_out: If a key is missing here, the code that displays labels has no name to show; how the caller handles this is not visible in this file.

summary: Holds shared fixed lists of company types and project roles, plus display labels for roles, for use by the front end and the back end.
purpose: Gives the app one set of allowed values so forms, displays and data checks use the same words.
why: The top comment says these lists are kept free of database code so the front end can use them directly.
how: Declares the allowed company types, then the allowed project roles, then a lookup table giving each role a readable name and a one-line definition. Nothing runs; the file only declares values.
inputs: None. The file reads no data.
outputs: Three fixed lists and one lookup table that other code reads.
risks: The full backend schema is a separate file and must match these lists by hand. The role lists also differ from the role lists in the industry settings file, and the code does not say which list governs which. The label table includes items that are not roles, such as association and media.
debug: If a role shows as a raw key, check that it has an entry in the label table. If a value is rejected, check it appears in the matching list. Compare with the backend schema and the industry settings file.
